title: OpenAWF Workflow
description: Structural schema for an OpenAWF workflow document. Non-normative: the specification prose is the source of truth. Some constraints (a start task that exists, edges that resolve to defined tasks, at least one terminal node) cannot be expressed here and are enforced by a conformant validator.

openawf.description: The OpenAWF version this document is written against.

model.description: The model every task runs on unless the task overrides it.

effort.description: The reasoning effort every task uses unless the task overrides it.

start.description: The name of the task the flow begins at.

orchestration.description: The task graph. Each key is a task name; its value is the node: the transition out of that task, plus optional per-node execution policy.

tasks.description: Task definitions keyed by name. Each entry is an inline task or a $ref to one.

mcp.description: Every MCP server the workflow's tasks call, keyed by server name. Credentials appear only as ${NAME} placeholders.

version.description: The workflow's version (identity). A human version string.

sha.description: Content hash of the workflow, algorithm-prefixed (e.g. sha256-...). null until sealed. Recomputed to verify the content is unchanged.

source.description: Where this workflow is fetched from (url, path, or registry id). Omitted when the workflow is authored in place rather than referenced.

metadata.description: Free keys describing the document, such as tags, authors and icon. Not used by execution.

model.description: One model as provider/name, or a list of them to try in order.

effort.description: How much reasoning a model spends on a task.

modelName.description: A model as provider/name, such as anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.

license.description: An SPDX license identifier, such as Apache-2.0.

externalVersion.description: A version identifier assigned by an external tool, such as an n8n versionId. Does not replace version or sha.

sha.description: A content hash, algorithm-prefixed, or null until sealed.

transition.description: Where a task goes next. null ends the flow; an edge is an unconditional transition; an object mapping outcomes to edges is a branch. An edge is a task name, or an object naming the task with per-edge execution policy.

edge.description: A single transition to a task. A bare string names the task; the object form names it under `task` and adds per-edge execution policy.

task.description: The task this edge transitions to.

retries.description: Attempts after the first failure before the task fails hard. null (the default) retries indefinitely; 0 means a single attempt.

session.description: How the task behaves when reached through this edge. "fresh" starts a new context; "resume" keeps the prior session's context.

branch.description: A map from each emitted outcome to the edge it takes. "task" is reserved (it marks an edge object), so no outcome may be named task.

ref.description: A reference to a task defined elsewhere (file path, URL, or id).

version.description: The task's version (identity). A human version string.

sha.description: Content hash of the task, algorithm-prefixed. null until sealed.

source.description: Where this task is fetched from (url, path, or registry id). Omitted when the task is authored in place.

input.description: JSON Schema the incoming data must satisfy. Absent when the task takes no input.

output.description: JSON Schema the task's output must satisfy. Absent when unconstrained.

model.description: Overrides the workflow model for this task.

effort.description: Overrides the workflow effort for this task.

outcomes.description: The outcomes this task may emit. Absent or empty when the task does not branch.

uses.description: The servers in mcp the task calls, and qualified tool names from them.

system.description: Standing instructions for the agent, in Markdown. May reference input fields as {{field}}.

body.description: The request for this step, in Markdown. May reference input fields as {{field}}.

mcpServer.description: An MCP server the workflow's tasks call. stdio servers take command, args and env. http and sse servers take url, headers and oauth.

type.description: The MCP transport. http is Streamable HTTP.

command.description: The executable that starts a stdio server.

env.description: Environment variables added to the runner's environment for the server process. They override variables of the same name.

url.description: The endpoint of an http or sse server.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent with every request.

allow.description: The tools the workflow may call. "*" (the default when omitted) allows every tool the server offers.

deny.description: The tools the workflow must not call.

timeout.description: The longest one tool call may run, in milliseconds.

oauth.description: OAuth client settings for an http or sse server.

client-id.description: The client ID registered with the authorization server.

callback-port.description: The local port of the redirect URI http://localhost:<port>/callback.

metadata-url.description: The authorization server's metadata URL. The runner uses it instead of discovering the metadata.
